name: Lana
headline: A person is more
than a symptom.
complaint: Since the ICU incident, the same scene returns in my dreams. At work I am always scanning for danger, and the alarms bring a wave of distress. I avoid the corridor where it happened. At home I feel emotionally numb and wake repeatedly through the night. My shifts keep changing, money is tight, and the support line has not called me back.

criteria.label: Distressing dreams
criteria.span: the same scene returns in my dreams

criteria.label: Cue-linked distress
criteria.span: the alarms bring a wave of distress

criteria.label: Reminder avoidance
criteria.span: avoid the corridor where it happened

networkNote: Sleep disruption and next-day distress co-vary in this simulated record.
gate: Confirm access, consent and stabilisation before considering intensive trauma work.
revision: Replace a fixed evening task with a cue that follows the end of each shift.

hapa.barrier: Rotating shifts disrupt a fixed routine.
hapa.when: After I get home from a shift
hapa.action: I will try a two-minute settling routine, then log how rested I feel.
hapa.coping: If the shift runs late, I will use the short version after changing clothes.
hapa.support: A care navigator helps arrange a trauma-informed appointment.
hapa.check: Track sleep disruption, cue distress and whether the plan felt manageable.

next: Carry forward sleep and distress signals; revisit shift-compatible support.
question: Which conditions make recovery possible?

name: Maarten
headline: The problem lives
between the branches.
complaint: My back pain makes me afraid to move, and I stop doing things I used to enjoy. The pain wakes me at night and leaves me exhausted in the day. It is becoming hard to do my job. When I lie down, I replay everything that went wrong and cannot shift my attention away. I worry about losing hours at work and paying for appointments.
person: Wants to remain active at work
context: Cost of care is a constraint

criteria.label: Activity avoidance
criteria.span: stop doing things I used to enjoy

criteria.label: Pain-related sleep loss
criteria.span: The pain wakes me at night

networkNote: The simulated pain-work relationship changes across heavier and lighter work periods.
gate: Check physical suitability with the treating professional before changing activity demands.
revision: Reduce the task demand and add a work-context feasibility check.

hapa.barrier: Heavy workdays make an ambitious plan impractical.
hapa.action: I will choose one manageable activity step agreed with my care professional.
hapa.coping: If demands are high, I will use the smaller agreed step and record the obstacle.
hapa.support: Discuss an adjustment request with an occupational support contact.
hapa.check: Track pain interference, movement confidence and work demands.

next: Refine the workload branch and retain the pain-sleep monitoring pair.
question: What changes when the working day changes?

name: Maya
headline: Start with her words.
Keep the whole context.
complaint: I keep worrying about what might happen if I fail. The same negative thoughts go round and round, and they interrupt my concentration. I struggle to stay engaged while studying and cannot filter out distractions. I wake again and again at night. I work evening shifts to cover rent, my deadlines overlap, and asking for support feels like another task.

criteria.label: Future-oriented worry
criteria.span: worrying about what might happen if I fail

criteria.label: Repetitive negative thinking
criteria.span: negative thoughts go round and round

criteria.label: Sustained engagement
criteria.span: struggle to stay engaged while studying

criteria.label: Interrupted sleep
criteria.span: wake again and again at night

networkNote: With this short simulated record, associations remain exploratory; no temporal model is claimed.
gate: Use a lower-complexity analysis while more observations accumulate.
revision: Keep the observation model small enough to fit the available record.

hapa.barrier: The plan feels too large to start during exam week.
hapa.action: I will choose one small task and note what makes starting difficult.
hapa.coping: If a shift changes my day, I will move the task to the next available block.
hapa.support: Identify one campus contact for practical or financial support.
hapa.check: Track worry, study engagement and the burden of check-ins.

next: Collect a longer record before considering a more complex network model.
question: How much can the available data really support?

name: Noor
headline: Support the person.
Account for the system.
complaint: Since taking on more care for my father, I feel close to burning out. I wake repeatedly during the night and feel tired all day. I keep imagining what could go wrong when I am away. The thoughts are hard to leave behind and make it difficult to concentrate at work. My siblings live far away, appointments keep shifting, and I rarely get uninterrupted time.

criteria.label: Anticipatory worry
criteria.span: imagining what could go wrong when I am away

criteria.label: Persistent rumination
criteria.span: thoughts are hard to leave behind

networkNote: A reduced contemporaneous network illustrates shared variation; direction is not established.
gate: Check practical support availability; avoid making self-management another unpaid demand.
revision: Add a support contact and shorten the task to fit an unpredictable care day.

hapa.barrier: Care demands interrupt planned recovery time.
hapa.action: I will identify one short recovery window and one person who can help protect it.
hapa.coping: If the handover is cancelled, I will ask for a smaller alternative window.
hapa.support: Agree one practical request with family or an available support service.
hapa.check: Track care demands, recovery opportunity and plan burden.

next: Reassess access to shared care and update the support-context links.
question: What if the barrier is outside the individual?

name: Elias
headline: Make room for meaning.
Find a workable next step.
complaint: Since my partner died, I long for them every day and struggle to accept that they are gone. Life feels without meaning, and I have pulled away from friends because of the loss. I avoid places that remind me of us. I wake before dawn and cannot settle back into the day. I live alone, the bus service is limited, and I do not want an app that asks too much.

criteria.label: Difficulty accepting loss
criteria.span: struggle to accept that they are gone

criteria.label: Social withdrawal
criteria.span: pulled away from friends because of the loss

criteria.label: Reminder avoidance
criteria.span: avoid places that remind me of us

networkNote: This sparse simulated record supports descriptive monitoring only, not a fitted network.
gate: Respect grief context and preference; symptom labels do not establish a grief disorder.
revision: Reduce check-in frequency and offer a non-digital route for the support contact.

hapa.barrier: Travel and digital burden make reconnection difficult.
hapa.when: At a time I choose this week
hapa.action: I will consider one meaningful contact, by phone or in person, at my own pace.
hapa.coping: If travel is difficult, I can choose a short telephone conversation instead.
hapa.support: Explore a practical bereavement support contact with consent.
hapa.check: Use brief, optional check-ins on connection, distress and sleep.

next: Retain descriptive monitoring and review preferred forms of contact.
question: Can the next step fit the life that remains?
